idiom_name: separate message record + System.Text.Json (source-generated context) + an explicit mapper class invoked by the queue handler
implementation_notes: The wire half belongs to the BCL: the message is a dedicated record, System.Text.Json serialises it (JsonSerializer.SerializeToUtf8Bytes / Deserialize), and a source-generated JsonSerializerContext keeps the mapping AOT-safe and trimming-friendly. The domain half stays explicit - a small OrderMessageMapper with ToMessage(Order) and FromMessage(OrderMessage), or extension methods next to the contract, called by the ServiceBusProcessor/queue handler - so no domain type carries wire attributes and no message type references domain behaviour. What replaces the classic mapper class is that static mapper plus the serializer's contract attributes; keep both in the messaging layer so the domain assembly does not reference System.Text.Json at all.
pitfalls: Serialising the entity 'for convenience' publishes navigation properties and couples the contract to the persistence shape; keep the message record free of domain types.
System.Text.Json matches property names case-insensitively and writes nulls by default: pin PropertyNamingPolicy and DefaultIgnoreCondition so the wire contract is the one you mapped.
Reflection-based (de)serialisation is trimmed away under AOT/trimming: declare a JsonSerializerContext rather than discovering the failure in production.
A message record captured by a long-lived handler can be mutated through `with`; treat mapped messages as values, not as shared state.
